channel.title: Online on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Online on Best of AI

item.title: Adyen
item.description: Adyen offers a single payments system that covers the entire flow, from the checkout page to the bank. It works as the payment processor and acquirer, which means it connects directly to card networks instead of relying on separate providers, and supports a wide range of payment methods including local options like iDEAL and Alipay. Large retailers, marketplaces, and subscription companies use it to accept payments in many countries with a unified view of the data.

item.title: Altium Designer
item.description:
Altium Designer is a professional environment for designing electronics. Engineers draw circuit schematics, lay out the physical board with components and traces, check the design against rules for manufacturing and signal integrity, and generate the files that fabricators need. It supports complex, high-speed, and multi-layer boards used in consumer devices, medical equipment, aerospace, and automotive electronics.

Collaboration and cloud tools extend the desktop product. Altium 365 provides a platform for sharing designs, managing components, and reviewing changes with teammates and manufacturers, and integrations with mechanical CAD allow electrical and mechanical engineers to work together. Component libraries and supply chain data help pick parts that are available. Newer features bring in AI-assisted capabilities, such as automating parts of layout or helping with design checks.

item.title: Auth0
item.description: Auth0 saves developers from building login systems themselves, which is a task where mistakes are costly. You add its SDK to an app, and it handles sign-up, login, password reset, social logins like Google or Apple, and passwordless options such as one-time codes and passkeys. It can connect to company identity providers for single sign-on, apply multi-factor and adaptive authentication, and manage roles and permissions. A hosted login page can be customized to match your brand.

item.title: Blackbaud
item.description:
Blackbaud is one of the largest vendors serving the social good sector. Its Raiser’s Edge NXT is a widely used fundraising and donor management system that tracks supporters, gifts, campaigns, and relationships, with tools for prospect research and online giving. Other products handle accounting, grants management, school administration, volunteer management, and corporate giving programs.

AI has been added across the line. Blackbaud Intelligence helps predict donors who are likely to give more, recommends who to contact, and drafts fundraising messages, and assistants help staff query data and build reports. Integrations connect with email, payment, and analytics tools. As a major data holder, Blackbaud has had to handle security responsibilities, including responding to a ransomware incident that affected customers.

item.title: Bumble
item.description:
Bumble set itself apart by changing who starts the conversation. When a man and a woman match, the woman has to send the first message within a time limit, which the company says reduces unwanted messages and gives women more control. In same-sex matches, either person can begin. The app uses the swipe format, and offers filters for interests, intentions, and distance.

Beyond dating, Bumble has modes to meet friends and to network professionally, though these have been less central to its success. Safety features include photo verification, a feature that detects and blurs unwanted nude images, and tools for reporting and blocking. AI is used to detect fake profiles, spam, and scams, and to flag harassing messages, which are persistent problems for dating apps.

item.title: CARTO
item.description:
CARTO focuses on location data at scale. Instead of copying data to a separate tool, it works where the data already lives, using the warehouse’s compute. Analysts can run spatial operations such as joins, clustering, and routing, and build interactive maps that stay connected to live data.

The platform has three common uses. Analysts build maps and dashboards to explore patterns, data teams construct workflows with a visual editor for spatial processing, and developers embed maps and analytics into applications through APIs. Datasets for demographics, points of interest, and mobility are available to enrich internal data. AI agents let users ask spatial questions in natural language.

item.title: CertiK
item.description:
CertiK works on security for blockchain projects. Its core service is the audit, in which engineers and automated tools review a project’s smart contract code to find bugs, logic mistakes, and vulnerabilities before funds are at risk. Audit reports are often published, and projects display them to build trust with users.

Beyond audits, CertiK offers monitoring and scoring. Its Skynet platform tracks security signals and rates projects, and it provides alerts, wallet and transaction analysis, and tools for investigating hacks. Bug bounty programs and penetration testing add other layers, and it also offers formal verification for high-assurance contracts.

item.title: Chainalysis
item.description:
Chainalysis makes sense of public blockchains. Cryptocurrency transactions are visible but pseudonymous, which makes it hard to know who is behind an address. Chainalysis clusters addresses, identifies services such as exchanges and mixers, and links activity to known entities using a large body of data and heuristics. Investigators can follow funds through a chain of transfers, and compliance teams can check whether a transaction touches risky or sanctioned counterparties.

Its products serve distinct users. Reactor is an investigation tool used by law enforcement and security teams, KYT (Know Your Transaction) monitors transactions for exchanges and financial institutions, and other tools support risk scoring, sanctions screening, and reporting. The company publishes research on crypto crime trends, which is widely cited. Machine learning helps detect patterns of illicit behavior and attribute clusters of activity.

item.title: CoachHub
item.description:
CoachHub is a digital coaching platform sold to employers. Employees are matched with certified coaches for one-on-one sessions on topics such as leadership, communication, and career growth. Sessions take place by video, and the company offers coaches across many countries and languages.

Between sessions, an AI coach named AIMY supports employees. It is available for quick conversations, helps rehearse difficult discussions, and supports goal setting, extending coaching beyond what a limited number of human sessions can cover. The platform reports on usage and progress to the sponsoring company.

item.title: Cvent
item.description:
Cvent is one of the most widely used enterprise event management suites. Planners create event websites and registration forms, collect payments, manage agendas and speakers, and communicate with attendees. A venue sourcing marketplace helps find hotels and meeting spaces and request proposals, which is a central part of corporate meeting planning, and tools handle housing blocks and travel for attendees.

On site and after the event, it provides engagement and measurement. Mobile apps, check-in, and badge printing run the day, while surveys and analytics measure attendance and satisfaction. AI features help generate event content, match attendees for networking, and assist with planning tasks, and integrations connect with CRMs and marketing automation to link events to pipeline. It supports in-person, virtual, and hybrid formats.

item.title: Dotmatics
item.description:
Dotmatics sells a connected software platform for laboratories. Scientists record experiments in electronic notebooks, manage samples and compounds, analyze results, and search data across projects. The aim is to link research data that would otherwise be spread across spreadsheets and separate instruments, so teams can find and reuse it.

The company has assembled a portfolio of well-known science tools. SnapGene supports molecular biology, GraphPad Prism is a standard for statistical analysis and graphs, Geneious handles sequence analysis, and other products cover chemistry, biology, and lab informatics. Machine learning and analytics features help with tasks such as modeling and data search.

item.title: Envision
item.description:
Envision uses AI to help blind and low-vision people with everyday visual tasks. Users point a phone or wearable camera at printed text, a product, or a scene and hear it read or described aloud. It can read documents, scan barcodes, recognize faces of saved contacts, and identify colors and objects.

The glasses offer hands-free use, with a camera worn at head level and spoken output, which suits tasks like reading mail or navigating a new place. An assistant lets users ask follow-up questions about what the camera sees, and a calling feature reaches sighted helpers when AI is not enough.

item.title: Finastra
item.description:
Finastra supplies the systems that sit behind a bank’s services. Its portfolio includes core banking platforms, commercial and retail lending, payments, trade finance, and treasury and capital markets tools. Banks of different sizes use it, from community institutions to global groups, and often run Finastra systems for decades.

The company has been moving customers toward the cloud and open banking. Its FusionFabric.cloud platform lets banks and third-party developers build apps and connect to Finastra’s services through APIs, and it has been adding AI features for tasks such as credit analysis, document processing, and customer service. Partnerships with large cloud providers support hosting.

item.title: Garmin Pilot
item.description:
Garmin Pilot covers the same ground as other flight apps. Pilots plan routes, get weather and notices to air missions, file flight plans, and carry charts and approach procedures on a tablet. In flight, it displays a moving map, traffic, and weather from compatible receivers.

Its advantage is integration with Garmin hardware. The app connects to Garmin avionics and portable devices, so flight plans can be sent to the aircraft’s navigator and data flows both ways. Features such as terrain awareness and flight data logging round out the toolset.

item.title: H&R Block
item.description:
H&R Block is one of the largest tax preparation brands in the United States. Customers can file themselves with online software, which asks questions, imports tax documents, and calculates returns, or go to one of thousands of offices where a tax professional prepares the return. A middle option connects people with an expert online who can answer questions or complete the return for them.

AI shows up as an assistant that answers tax questions in plain language, helps find deductions and credits, and explains forms, working within the tax software and drawing on the company’s tax knowledge. Other features include importing prior-year returns, audit support, and refund tracking. The company also provides services such as small business tax and bookkeeping.

item.title: Icertis
item.description:
Icertis helps big companies manage a very large volume of contracts. Its platform stores contracts in a central repository, supports authoring from templates and clause libraries, routes agreements for approval, and tracks obligations after signing, so deadlines and commitments are not missed. Customers use it for sales, procurement, partner, and employment agreements across many countries.

AI is a core part of the pitch. The Icertis Contract Intelligence platform reads agreements to extract key terms, flags risky or nonstandard language, and compares contracts against playbooks. Generative AI features answer questions about a contract portfolio, summarize agreements, and assist with drafting, and the company has expanded its capabilities through acquisitions. It integrates with enterprise systems such as Salesforce, SAP, and Microsoft.

item.title: Infura
item.description:
Infura gives developers a dependable way to talk to blockchains. Running a node means maintaining servers, storage, and synchronization, so many projects prefer to use an API instead. Infura offers JSON-RPC and WebSocket endpoints for Ethereum, layer 2 networks, and other chains, letting apps read data, send transactions, and subscribe to events through a single key.

The service includes extras. Support for IPFS provides decentralized file storage, and features such as gas estimation and network monitoring help developers. Because Infura is part of Consensys, which also makes MetaMask, it is deeply integrated into much of the Ethereum ecosystem, and a lot of wallets and applications depend on it.

item.title: KAYAK
item.description:
KAYAK doesn’t sell travel itself. Instead, it searches airlines, online travel agencies, and hotel sites at once and shows the options in one place, with filters for price, stops, airlines, and times. When you pick an option, it sends you to the provider to book. This saves time compared with checking many sites individually, and the interface offers flexible date grids and nearby airport searches to find cheaper alternatives.

Several tools help with timing and decisions. Price alerts notify you when a fare changes, and forecasts indicate whether prices are likely to rise or fall, so you can choose between booking now or waiting. KAYAK also offers trip planning, a Trips organizer for itineraries, and filters for things like total cost including bag fees. Conversational AI search lets you describe a trip in plain language and get suggestions.

item.title: MasterControl
item.description:
MasterControl serves regulated manufacturers, such as pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. Its quality management system handles documents, training, change control, deviations, and corrective actions in a way that satisfies FDA and international rules. Electronic records and signatures provide the audit trail regulators expect.

The platform extends to manufacturing. Electronic batch records and production tools capture how products are made, connecting quality data to the shop floor. AI features help review documents, find trends in quality events, and speed up routine tasks.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID
item.description:
Entra ID is the identity system behind most Microsoft cloud accounts. When someone signs in to Microsoft 365, Teams, or Azure, Entra ID checks who they are and what they may access. It provides single sign-on to thousands of third-party apps, manages users and groups, and supports multi-factor authentication, passwordless sign-in with passkeys and authenticator apps, and device registration.

The security features are a key reason companies use it. Conditional Access policies decide when to allow, block, or challenge sign-ins based on conditions such as location, device health, and risk level. Identity Protection uses machine learning to detect risky sign-ins and compromised accounts, and governance tools handle access reviews, entitlement management, and privileged access. It extends to customers and partners through external identity features, and increasingly to non-human identities such as apps and AI agents.

item.title: Motive
item.description:
Motive started as KeepTruckin with electronic logging devices that record drivers’ hours, which US regulations require for many commercial trucks. It expanded into a fleet platform with GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, and tools for compliance, dispatching, and maintenance, serving trucking companies, construction firms, and other businesses with vehicles on the road.

AI dashcams are a major product. A camera facing the road and the driver uses computer vision to detect events such as distracted driving, phone use, following too closely, and rolling stops, and alerts drivers in real time while sending clips to managers for coaching. Safety scoring, reports, and exoneration video after accidents help reduce incidents and insurance costs. The company also offers a fleet card and spend controls.

item.title: Nansen
item.description:
Nansen turns raw blockchain data into readable information. Every wallet on a public chain is an anonymous string of characters, so Nansen builds a database of labels, tagging wallets that belong to exchanges, funds, protocols, and traders with a track record. Seeing that a labeled fund bought a token is more informative than seeing an unknown address.

Dashboards track token flows, new token launches, NFT activity, and the holdings of tagged wallets. Alerts notify users when watched wallets move funds, and analytical tools help researchers study a project’s holders and trading patterns. An AI assistant answers questions about on-chain data in plain language, and it supports many chains.

item.title: Oura Ring
item.description:
Oura packs sensors into a ring that is comfortable to wear day and night. It tracks sleep stages, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, body temperature, and movement, then gives scores for sleep and readiness that suggest how hard to push each day. Many people choose it for sleep tracking, since a ring is less obtrusive than a watch in bed, and battery life lasts several days.

The app presents trends and offers guidance. Features cover cycle and fertility insights, stress and recovery information, activity goals, and workouts. An AI advisor lets users ask questions about their data in plain language and receive personalized suggestions. Oura works with Apple Health, Google Health Connect, and other apps, and it has partnered with companies in areas like glucose monitoring.

item.title: Sardine
item.description:
Sardine is a fraud and compliance platform for financial services. It collects signals about the device and the way a user interacts, such as typing patterns and whether a session looks automated, and combines them with transaction data to score the risk of an account opening, a payment, or a login. Decisions happen in milliseconds, so legitimate customers face little friction.

The platform covers a range of risk. It addresses account takeover, payment fraud, scams, and identity fraud, and integrates with know your customer and anti-money laundering workflows. AI agents help compliance teams by gathering evidence, reviewing alerts, and drafting case notes, which reduces the manual work behind investigations.

item.title: Shortform
item.description:
Shortform sits between a short summary and the book itself. Each guide covers a book’s ideas in depth, adds analysis comparing it with other books, and includes exercises that help readers apply the lessons. Readers can use them to decide what to read in full or to review a book they have finished.

The library spans business, psychology, history, and self-help, and includes guides to classic works and some articles and fiction. AI features offer a chat assistant for asking questions about a guide.

item.title: SnapGene
item.description:
SnapGene gives molecular biologists a visual, reliable way to plan DNA work. Researchers open or create plasmid and DNA sequences, see features such as genes and promoters automatically annotated, and simulate cloning steps like restriction digests, ligations, Gibson assembly, and Gateway cloning before going to the bench. The tool shows resulting maps and sequences, helping avoid costly mistakes.

It has a large library of standard vectors and features, tools for designing primers, and a viewer that lets collaborators open files without a license. Sequence comparison, alignments, and the ability to import from databases support daily lab tasks. Files are shared in a format that is widely used across the field. A server version supports team libraries.

item.title: The Batch
item.description: The Batch is a free weekly newsletter for people who follow AI. Each issue begins with a letter from Andrew Ng, a leading AI researcher and educator, sharing his perspective on a current topic, such as how teams should build with AI or what trends matter. That is followed by several concise news items on research, products, policy, and industry developments, each with a clear explanation and links to sources.

item.title: Tinder
item.description: Tinder popularized the swipe. You see a profile with photos and a short bio, swipe right to like or left to pass, and if the other person also likes you, you match and can message. The format is fast and casual, which fits its large, young user base across many countries. People use it for dating, relationships, and meeting new people, and settings let you filter by distance, age, and gender preferences.

item.title: Tractive
item.description:
Tractive helps owners keep track of their pets. A small GPS device attached to a collar sends the animal’s location to a phone app via cellular networks, so you can see where your dog or cat is in real time, view recent routes, and set virtual fences that trigger alerts if the pet leaves a defined area. A light and sound function helps find a pet at night.

Beyond location, the devices monitor activity, sleep, and behavior, and some models track signs of health changes such as excessive scratching or licking. Data shows trends and can help owners share information with veterinarians. Features such as a lost-pet mode, sharing access with family, and integration with pet services support everyday use.

item.title: Trimble Construction
item.description:
Trimble is a major technology supplier to the construction industry. Its portfolio includes software for estimating costs, scheduling, managing projects and finances, coordinating building models, and running equipment. SketchUp and Tekla, used for design and structural detailing, are part of the group, and Trimble Connect provides a collaboration space for project data.

Its hardware is a distinctive strength. Survey instruments, GPS and GNSS receivers, and machine control systems guide excavators and other equipment based on a 3D model, linking digital plans to work on the ground. Integrating these systems with software lets data flow from the model to the field and back as built information. AI features assist with planning, quantity takeoff, and analyzing project data.

item.title: UserWay
item.description:
UserWay is a web accessibility service. Its widget gives visitors controls to adjust text size, contrast, spacing, and animations, and it applies automated fixes such as adding missing labels. A scanner checks pages against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and reports issues, so site owners can see problems and prioritize them.

For deeper work, UserWay offers managed services with human experts who audit and fix content, plus tools for documents and PDFs. Reports and accessibility statements help show good faith efforts toward compliance. The product works with common platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, and Wix.

item.title: Wisdom Panel
item.description:
Wisdom Panel offers genetic testing for dogs and cats. An owner swabs the pet’s cheek, mails the sample, and receives a report on breed ancestry, family tree, and traits. The report also screens for genetic health conditions the pet may carry or be at risk for, which can inform decisions with a veterinarian.

The company draws on a large database of breed samples and research, and sells tests through retailers, directly to owners, and through veterinary clinics. Health screening results are meant to start conversations with a vet, and some conditions come with guidance on diet or monitoring. The brand belongs to Mars Petcare, which also owns other pet care businesses.

item.title: Dental Monitoring
item.description:
Dental Monitoring lets orthodontists check on patients remotely. A patient attaches a small cheek retractor to a phone, scans their teeth on a schedule, and uploads the images. The software compares scans to the treatment plan and measures how teeth are moving.

AI flags problems such as aligners that do not fit, lost attachments, hygiene concerns, or progress that is behind schedule. The orthodontist reviews alerts and decides whether to adjust the plan, send the next aligners earlier, or schedule a visit. This can reduce in-person appointments and catch issues sooner.

item.title: ForeFlight
item.description:
ForeFlight is an app for planning and flying. Pilots build routes, check weather and airspace, file flight plans, and view approach plates and charts. In the air, it shows moving maps and traffic and weather from compatible receivers, which replaces paper charts.

Weather is a big part. Layers show forecasts, radar, and hazards, and tools highlight conditions most likely to affect a given route. Performance and weight and balance planning help with safety, and integrations connect to avionics and tablets. Teams in flight departments use it to share data.

item.title: Greenlight Guru
item.description:
Greenlight Guru serves a heavily regulated industry. Medical device makers must document how a product was designed, how risks were assessed, and how problems are corrected. The platform organizes these records, links requirements to risks and tests, and keeps them audit ready, replacing documents scattered in shared drives.

Modules cover design controls, risk management, document control, training, supplier management, and corrective and preventive actions. AI features help draft documents and risk analyses and answer questions about regulations, saving time on repetitive writing. A clinical module supports post-market work.

item.title: Instrumentl
item.description:
Instrumentl is a grant discovery and management platform. A nonprofit describes its mission and programs, and the system recommends foundation and government grants that fit, with details on the funder’s giving history, typical award sizes, and past recipients. Alerts notify the team when new matches appear.

Once a grant is identified, a tracker handles tasks, deadlines, reports, and documents for each application, with collaboration for the team. AI assists with research, summarizing funder priorities and drafting parts of proposals, though grant writing still depends on strong program knowledge.

item.title: Mentalyc
item.description:
Mentalyc is an AI note-taking tool for mental health professionals. A therapist records a session, uploads audio, or enters brief notes, and the tool generates a structured progress note that matches the format their practice uses. The clinician edits and approves it.

The product emphasizes privacy, since therapy content is sensitive. It states that it follows health privacy rules and offers controls such as removing identifying details. It also supports treatment plans and can learn a therapist’s style over time.

item.title: Notarize (Proof)
item.description:
Notarize brought notarization online. A signer uploads a document, verifies identity by scanning an ID and answering questions, joins a video call with a commissioned notary, and signs digitally. The notary applies a digital seal and the document is stored securely, making a process that required an in-person visit possible from home.

The company, now operating as Proof, expanded into broader identity and signature products for businesses, including title and escrow, banks, and real estate. AI-based checks examine ID documents and confirm that a live person is present, which helps resist fraud.

item.title: Tracers
item.description:
Tracers is an investigative data service. A user enters a name, address, or other identifier, and the platform returns linked records about people and businesses, such as addresses, relatives, liens, and court filings. Matching algorithms connect pieces of information.

Customers include private investigators, attorneys, collections agencies, and law enforcement. Access is restricted by law in many cases and requires a permissible purpose, and results have limits in accuracy.

Tracers is sold on subscription and per search. Using such data raises privacy and legal issues, and background checks used for employment or housing are subject to consumer reporting laws. Alternatives include LexisNexis Accurint, TLOxp, Thomson Reuters CLEAR, and IRB Search. Tracers suits licensed investigative professionals.

item.title: Upheal
item.description:
Upheal helps therapists reduce paperwork. With client consent, the tool records or transcribes a session and drafts a note in the clinician’s preferred format, which they review and sign. It can summarize progress over time and suggest treatment plan updates.

The product emphasizes privacy and compliance with health data rules, and offers a free tier for solo practitioners. Session insights, such as talk time and themes, give feedback to the clinician.

item.title: Wildbook
item.description:
Wildbook turns photos into population data. Scientists and citizen scientists upload pictures of animals such as whale sharks, giraffes, and sea turtles, and the software recognizes individuals by distinctive markings, such as spot patterns or fin shapes, and links sightings over time.

That reveals movement, survival, and population size without physically tagging animals. The platform supports many species, with separate databases for each, and photos from tourists and social media can contribute.

item.title: NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform
item.description:
The platform responds to a security worry: autonomous agents that can run commands and access data need limits that a compromised agent cannot disable. OpenShell is an open-source runtime that places each agent in its own sandbox with policy-based permissions, and a prover checks that granted permissions cannot combine into something the operator did not intend.

Sentry adds enforcement outside the agent’s machine. It runs on BlueField data processing units, which sit apart from the host, so it can watch behavior and isolate an agent quickly even if the host is compromised. NVIDIA has described it as a reference design, with many partners integrating the pieces.

item.title: Cellebrite
item.description:
Cellebrite is a digital forensics company. Its tools pull data from mobile devices, cloud accounts, and computers, including deleted items where possible, and organize it so investigators can review messages, photos, locations, and app activity. The company serves police, intelligence agencies, and corporate security teams.

Analysis products help investigators manage large amounts of data. AI can classify images, search through text, find connections between people and devices, and build timelines. Cloud platforms support collaboration across a case and sharing evidence with prosecutors.

item.title: Crisalix
item.description:
Crisalix builds simulation tools for aesthetic medicine. A surgeon takes photos of a patient, the software builds a 3D model of the face or body, and the surgeon adjusts parameters to show what a procedure might look like. Patients can see and discuss options before deciding.

The aim is to improve communication and set realistic expectations. A visual helps patients and surgeons align on goals, and consultations can be more productive. The company sells to plastic surgeons, dermatologists, and clinics, and has tools for marketing and patient engagement.

item.title: ESHA Genesis R&D
item.description:
Genesis R&D is a long-standing tool for food product development. A formulator enters ingredients and amounts, and the software calculates nutrients using a large food database, then generates a nutrition facts panel and an ingredient list formatted for regulatory requirements in different countries.

It also helps with design choices. Users can compare formulas, adjust ingredients to hit targets for calories, sodium, or protein, check claims such as low fat or high fiber, and flag allergens. These features reduce the risk of labeling errors, which can lead to recalls.

item.title: Givebutter
item.description:
Givebutter is a fundraising platform for nonprofits. Organizations create donation forms, run crowdfunding and peer-to-peer campaigns, sell event tickets, and accept recurring gifts. Its donor CRM keeps a record of each supporter’s giving and communications.

The platform tries to be affordable for small groups. It has been known for a model where donors can choose to tip the platform rather than the nonprofit paying fees. Auctions, text-to-give, and email tools are included. AI helps segment lists and draft appeals and thank-yous.

item.title: Holistiplan
item.description:
Holistiplan helps financial advisors use tax returns in planning. An advisor uploads a client’s return, and the software extracts the figures and generates a summary showing income, deductions, brackets, and observations. It highlights ideas worth discussing, such as Roth conversions, capital gains harvesting, or the timing of donations.

Scenarios let advisors model the effect of a strategy on taxes. Reports are designed to be shared with clients, helping advisors show value beyond investments. AI assists with reading documents and drafting talking points.

item.title: accessiBe
item.description:
accessiBe promises to make websites more accessible with minimal effort. A line of code adds an accessibility interface for visitors, with options such as larger text, contrast adjustments, and keyboard navigation, while AI runs in the background to detect issues like missing image descriptions and improper labels and attempt to fix them. Businesses use it to reduce the risk of accessibility lawsuits and to serve users with disabilities.

The company has built other products, including audits, monitoring, and expert-assisted remediation. It reports compliance status and offers statements that businesses can publish. Its marketing emphasized automation and quick compliance.

item.title: AutoGrid
item.description:
AutoGrid builds software for the changing electricity grid. As more homes and businesses add solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicles, utilities need ways to coordinate them. AutoGrid’s platform forecasts supply and demand, controls devices, and combines many small resources into virtual power plants that can respond when the grid needs help. Machine learning predicts energy use and optimizes when to charge, discharge, or reduce load.

Utilities and energy retailers use it to run demand response programs, manage commercial and residential batteries, and monetize flexibility in energy markets. It integrates with device makers and energy management systems, so a single platform can orchestrate thermostats, batteries, EV chargers, and industrial loads. The goal is to lower costs and reduce the need for new power plants during peak demand.

item.title: Cronometer
item.description:
Cronometer is for people who want to know what is in their food, not only how much of it they eat. You log meals by searching a database, scanning barcodes, or entering recipes, and the app breaks them down into calories, macronutrients, and dozens of micronutrients. Its data comes from verified sources such as government nutrition databases, which makes it more reliable than apps built mostly on user-submitted entries.

Detailed tracking supports use cases like managing a medical diet, checking for vitamin and mineral gaps, tracking fasting or specific eating plans, and training for sports. Targets can be customized, charts show trends, and the app can connect with fitness trackers and devices to account for activity. Newer features use AI to speed up logging, for example by recognizing foods from photos, though human review is wise.

item.title: Embark Veterinary
item.description: Embark’s test starts with a cheek swab at home. You activate the kit, collect a sample from your dog, and mail it to the lab, and results arrive online in a few weeks. The breed report shows a percentage breakdown across hundreds of breeds and how far back each breed appears in the family tree, which owners of mixed-breed dogs often find revealing. It also estimates traits such as coat color and weight.

item.title: Grip
item.description:
Grip focuses on a problem every large event has: people attend hoping to meet the right contacts, then wander the floor without finding them. Grip collects attendees’ goals when they register, such as buying a product, finding partners, or recruiting, and uses matchmaking to recommend whom to meet. People can accept suggestions, message one another, and schedule meetings before and during the event.

Organizers get tools to manage the experience. Exhibitors can see qualified leads and capture them at the booth, sponsors get measurable engagement data, and the event team can track how many meetings happened and how satisfied participants were. A mobile app and integrations with registration systems, CRMs, and event platforms connect the pieces. Typical customers are trade show and conference organizers in industries like technology, healthcare, and manufacturing.

item.title: Jumio
item.description: Jumio helps businesses confirm that a customer is who they claim to be. A user photographs an ID document, such as a passport or driver’s license, and takes a selfie. Jumio checks the document for authenticity, reads the data, compares the selfie to the photo on the ID, and uses liveness detection to make sure a real person is present, not a photo, video, or deepfake. The process takes seconds and replaces in-person checks.

item.title: Meta Quest
item.description:
Meta Quest headsets made virtual reality mainstream by removing the need for cables and a powerful computer. The headsets have built-in processors, controllers, and cameras that track your hands and surroundings, and run apps from the Quest store. The latest models support mixed reality, blending virtual objects with the live view of the room, which opens up games and tools that interact with your space.

The ecosystem includes a wide range of experiences. Popular uses include games, fitness apps, social worlds, watching videos on virtual screens, and creating or collaborating in 3D. Meta is adding AI features, including Meta AI as a voice assistant and tools that help creators build worlds, and headsets can connect to a PC for more demanding games. Models vary in price and capability, and the software is called Horizon OS.

item.title: Noom
item.description:
Noom approaches weight loss as a behavior change problem. After a quiz about your habits and goals, the app builds a plan and delivers short daily lessons based on cognitive behavioral therapy, covering topics like emotional eating, habits, and triggers. A food log uses a color system for food density instead of strict calorie bans, and the app tracks weight, steps, and water.

Support comes through coaching and community. Depending on the plan, users can message a coach, join groups, and use an AI assistant to ask questions and get guidance. Noom has expanded into medical weight management, offering clinician-supervised programs that may include prescription medication in some regions. Programs are meant to help people form sustainable habits.

item.title: Palmetto
item.description:
Palmetto connects homeowners with solar and energy services. A homeowner enters an address and gets an assessment of how much a system could save, compares financing options, and is matched with installers. The company also offers energy management that coordinates devices like batteries and EV chargers.

On the business side, Palmetto provides software and data used by installers, utilities, and fintechs, including tools for sizing systems, tracking incentives, and managing projects. AI helps optimize when to charge or use stored energy based on rates and weather.

item.title: PromptBase
item.description:
PromptBase turned prompts into products. Creators craft prompts that reliably produce a type of result, such as a particular art style, a logo format, or a structured business document, and list them with example outputs. Buyers pay a small amount to get the text, then use it with the relevant AI tool, saving time on trial and error.

The marketplace organizes prompts by model and category, shows sample images, and uses ratings and reviews to help buyers choose. It also supports custom prompt requests and tools for prompt creators to test and sell their work. The business sits on a belief that skilled prompting has value, particularly for image generators where small wording changes make a big difference.

item.title: Teladoc Health
item.description:
Teladoc Health delivers healthcare through phones and video. Members can see a clinician for common conditions, get prescriptions where appropriate, and access specialists, therapists, and dermatologists without traveling. Employers and health plans buy the service for their members, which makes access fast and convenient for non-emergency issues, and it includes expert medical opinion services and virtual nursing.

The company also runs programs for chronic conditions, such as diabetes and hypertension, combining connected devices, coaching, and digital tools. Mental health care is a major area, including its consumer therapy brand BetterHelp. AI is used for matching patients with providers, supporting clinicians with documentation, and personalizing care programs.

item.title: Tripadvisor
item.description:
Tripadvisor built its name on traveler reviews. Visitors rate and describe hotels, restaurants, tours, and sights, and the site ranks places based on those opinions, which people use to decide where to stay and eat. Photos, forums, and Q&A add detail. It covers millions of places worldwide and is free to browse.

The site has developed into a booking and planning platform. It compares hotel prices and links to booking partners, sells tours and activities through Viator, and supports restaurant reservations through TheFork. AI trip-planning features create itineraries from a short description, suggest places based on reviews, and organize saved items into trips. Businesses use Tripadvisor to manage their listings, respond to reviews, and advertise.

item.title: TurboTax
item.description: TurboTax makes tax filing a guided interview. You answer plain-language questions, import documents like W-2s and 1099s, and the software fills in the forms, checks for errors, and estimates your refund or amount owed. It supports many situations, from simple returns to investments, self-employment, and rental income, and e-files returns with federal and state tax agencies. It has long been the most recognized brand in consumer tax software in the U.S.

item.title: Woebot
item.description:
Woebot was one of the best-known mental health chatbots. It talked with users about mood and thoughts, using techniques from cognitive behavioral therapy to help them notice patterns, challenge unhelpful beliefs, and practice coping skills. Conversations were short and structured, with a friendly tone, so people could use it when they felt stressed or anxious, at any time of day.

It differed from general chatbots by using carefully written, clinically reviewed content instead of free-form generation, and the company ran studies to evaluate it. It aimed to make support more accessible and affordable than traditional therapy, and was used by individuals, employers, and health systems. It was always described as a supplement to, not a replacement for, professional care.

item.title: Wysa
item.description: Wysa is a conversational app for stress, low mood, and anxiety. Users chat with a friendly penguin character that asks about how they feel and offers exercises, such as reframing negative thoughts, breathing techniques, sleep tools, and guided meditations. The responses draw on structured therapeutic content written and reviewed by clinicians instead of unconstrained text generation, which is meant to make it safer and more predictable than a general chatbot.

item.title: Zebra Medical Vision
item.description:
Zebra Medical Vision developed AI that reads medical scans and flags findings. Its algorithms examined chest X-rays, CT scans, and mammograms for conditions such as lung nodules, bone density loss, fatty liver, coronary calcium, and signs of fractures, often picking up incidental findings that a radiologist focused on another question might not report. The company had several algorithms cleared by regulators in the United States and Europe.

A distinctive aspect was population health analysis: by screening scans that were already taken for other purposes, hospitals could identify patients at risk of conditions such as osteoporosis or cardiovascular disease and follow up. Zebra Medical Vision offered its tools through a cloud platform that integrated with radiology workflows.

item.title: ContractSafe
item.description:
ContractSafe addresses a basic business problem: contracts scattered across inboxes, shared drives, and filing cabinets. Teams upload agreements into one searchable repository, and the system reads them to pull out key details such as parties, effective dates, renewal terms, and notice periods. Because the text is searchable, finding a specific clause across hundreds of contracts takes seconds instead of hours.

Automation helps avoid missed deadlines. ContractSafe can send alerts before a contract renews or expires, so teams can renegotiate or cancel in time instead of being locked into automatic renewals. Permissions control who can see sensitive agreements, and reports summarize the portfolio by type, value, and upcoming dates. Integrations connect with tools such as Salesforce and Microsoft or Google storage, and an audit trail records activity.

item.title: Ghostwall
item.description:
Ghostwall belongs to the group of click fraud prevention tools. Advertisers who pay per click can lose money when bots or competitors click ads. The service watches traffic to paid campaigns, looks for suspicious patterns, and blocks the sources that appear fraudulent, for example by adding them to exclusion lists on ad platforms.

Reports show blocked clicks and estimated savings. The ad platforms filter some invalid traffic themselves, so independent tools add value mainly for accounts with significant spend or visible fraud problems. Results depend on how good the detection is, and aggressive blocking can also exclude real customers.
